data.gender_notes: Adriella is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Adriella is a feminine Latin name derived from Hadriana, a feminine form of Hadrian, which means 'dark one' or 'man's woman'. In ancient Rome, Hadrian was a renowned emperor known for his extensive travels to maintain the Roman Empire. The name has a rich historical and cultural significance. The name Adriella carries the meaning “Man's woman, dark one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Adriella usually hope their child will grow to embody man's woman, dark one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Adrielle, the daughter of the Roman consul Publius Valerius Publicola, was traditionally believed to have been the first Christian martyr in Rome. According to legend, she was a young virgin who refused to sacrifice to the pagan gods in honor of Emperor Nero's birthday. She was put in a red-hot brass bull and thrown into the Tiber River. Miraculously, she survived and was later beheaded. Her feast day is celebrated on February 3.

Adrielle de la Marche, also known as Adelaide of the Marches, was a duchess of Normandy in the 11th century. She was the daughter of Count William I of Normandy and was noted for her piety and charitable works. She founded several monasteries and hospitals, and was venerated as a saint after her death.
